headline: Bull's safety exit is too close, the desk's replays hit it first 71 times out of 100, and the bounce signals Bull cited have already moved, so skip.

messages.reply_to: Bull: buy near $170.80, get out if it drops to $169.40
messages.text: The desk checked this plan. Nvidia normally moves about $3.85 in an hour, but your safety exit is only $1.40 away. That is about a third of a normal hourly move, so ordinary wiggles could kick you out.

messages.reply_to: Bull: Targets give roughly 1.6 and 2.8 reward for each 1 of risk
messages.text: The math is right, but the odds are not. The desk replayed the day 10,000 times: the first goal came first only 19 times out of 100, the safety exit came first 71 times. In real history it was 8 wins against 31 stops.

messages.reply_to: Bull: RSI is 28... sellers are worn out
messages.text: Low RSI only says it fell fast. The hourly score is 28.4 and the 5-minute is 27.4. On every chart the fast average line is still under the slow one, and the hourly selling-pressure gauge is still negative.

messages.reply_to: Bull: Price is also sitting at the bottom edge of its normal range
messages.text: Not anymore. The 5-minute bottom edge has moved down to $170.26 and the 15-minute one is at $172.11, so price at $171.50 sits below the 15-minute edge. In a falling stock the bottom edge keeps getting walked down.

messages.reply_to: Bull: UK brokers saw buying jump 274% to 432%
messages.text: That is everyday investors buying the dip, and I could not open that page myself. Early dip buyers get hurt if the news gets worse, and the board's probe has no result yet.

messages.reply_to: Bull: That is a one-person worry, not a problem with Nvidia's chips
messages.text: The one person is the CEO. Earnings are Nov 17, and three House chairs asked him to brief them on Nov 18. No calendar shows surprise headlines, so 'CLEAR' is not the same as safe.

messages.reply_to: Bull: the sell-off is about the story, not the industry
messages.text: I agree it is Nvidia's own problem. That is my point: a company-specific cloud does not clear because the sector rises. It clears when the board reports.

argument:
Plan math (desk_r1): entry 170.80, stop 169.40, targets 173.00 and 174.65. Risk is 1.40 per share, rewards 2.20 and 3.85, so 1.57R and 2.75R. Fine on paper, but the stop is 0.36x the 1h ATR (3.85). Bull's 1.1x used the 5m ATR, which the Judge marked wrong for this window. The Time Machine (10,000 replays, 60 days of 5m bars) gives: target first 19.2%, stop first 71.4%, neither 9.4%, average result -0.395R. Real history of the same distances (59 past days): 8 target, 31 stop, 20 neither. Verdict: STRONG_STOP.

Bull's bounce signals have moved. Fresh 14:55 data shows 5m RSI 27.4 (Bull used 28.1, the saved snapshot said 25.1), 15m 29.7, 1h 28.4. The 5m lower Bollinger is 170.26 (not 169.94) and the 15m lower band is 172.11, above the live price of 171.50. Bull's 5m EMA9 target is now 173.25, but 5m EMA21 is 174.97 and SMA50 176.45, so the path up passes several resistance lines. The 1h MACD histogram is still negative (-0.35). Price is below VWAP 171.75.

On the news: the board's independent committee is investigating Huang and has published no findings; earnings come Nov 17 and a closed-door House briefing is requested for Nov 18 (CNBC). Bull's retail-buying evidence is a headline I could not verify, and heavy retail dip buying is not proof of a bottom. I am dropping my own Round 1 claims about a shareholder lawsuit, a possible subpoena and the Polymarket 18% line: they rested on snippets or a single article, so I do not lean on them.

Plain summary: even on Bull's own numbers, the stop is too tight and the replays say the stop is far more likely to be hit than the first target.

evidence.claim: Desk check of Bull's plan: stop 0.36x the 1h ATR (3.8564); R multiples 1.571 and 2.75; replays target first 19.17%, stop first 71.43%, neither 9.4%, avg R -0.395; history 8 target / 31 stop / 20 neither of 59
evidence.plain: The safety exit is too close and, in 10,000 replays, it gets hit about 3.7 times as often as the first goal.
evidence.source: Desk (desk_r1.json, Time Machine on Yahoo 5m bars)

evidence.claim: Fresh data at 14:55:52Z: price 171.50, -4.01%; VWAP 171.75; 5m RSI 27.4, 15m 29.7, 1h 28.4; 5m Bollinger lower 170.26; 15m lower 172.11; 5m EMA9 173.25, EMA21 174.97; 1h ATR 3.8499; 1h MACD histogram -0.355; EMA9 under EMA21 and price under SMA50/SMA200 on 5m, 15m, 1h
evidence.plain: Nvidia is still under all its average lines. The 'bottom edge of range' Bull used has moved, and price is below the 15-minute edge.

evidence.claim: Three House Republican chairs asked Huang to a closed-door briefing on Nov 18, a day after Q3 earnings; board announced an independent investigation Sunday
evidence.plain: The CEO story has dates on it inside the next 8 days, and the board has not given results yet.
evidence.source: CNBC (page fetched; earnings date implied by 'a day after earnings')

evidence.claim: Search coverage: board committee with outside counsel investigating, no findings published, Huang remains CEO, no criminal charges reported; earnings Nov 17
evidence.plain: Nothing is settled. Good or bad news could arrive any time.
evidence.source: Web search summary of Fox Business / CNBC / FourWeekMBA (snippet only)

evidence.claim: Event guard CLEAR: only medium-impact items (10-year note auction 18:00Z, poultry report 17:00Z, crude stocks 21:30Z); the CEO probe is not on any calendar
evidence.plain: The calendar being quiet does not cover surprise news about the CEO.

evidence.claim: 52-week low $164.27 vs live price 171.50; day low 170.12; day high 174.65; day volume 79.9M
evidence.plain: The yearly low is only about 4% below. The first goal ($173) needs a move past several falling average lines.

rebuttals.response: Used the 5m ATR. On the 1h ATR the desk gets 0.36x, flagged stop_tight. Replays hit the stop first 71% of the time.
Math is right (1.571R, 2.75R) but the first target is reached first only 19% of the time and the second only about 5%. Average result is -0.395R.

rebuttals.opponent_point: Bull: RSI 28 means sellers are worn out
rebuttals.response: RSI under 30 shows the speed of the fall, not its end. 5m RSI is 27.4 now, the 1h MACD histogram is still negative, and price is under VWAP.

rebuttals.opponent_point: Bull: price at lower Bollinger band 169.94
rebuttals.response: Stale. The 5m band is 170.26 and the 15m band is 172.11, so price is under the 15m band, which shows the downtrend, not a floor.
Retail dip-buying is not proof of a bottom; I could not verify the page. Dip buyers are often early in news-driven falls.

rebuttals.opponent_point: Bull: event guard CLEAR, so no big news in window
rebuttals.response: The guard only knows scheduled macro data. The board probe, the House request (Nov 18) and earnings (Nov 17) are real headline risk that can hit at any minute.

plan_flaws: Stop 169.40 is 0.36x the 1h ATR (desk stop_tight); Bull's 1.1x used the 5m ATR
Time Machine: target first 19.2% vs stop first 71.4%, avg R -0.395; history 8 targets vs 31 stops of 59
Entry 170.80 is a limit below live 171.50 (0.44% away, 0.19 ATR): it may never fill, or fill only on a further slide
Target 173.00 sits under the 5m EMA21 (174.97); the second needs the day high 174.65 against VWAP and a falling SMA50
Bull's Bollinger 169.94 and RSI 28.1 figures are stale against the 14:55 data (170.26 and 27.4)
plan_flaws_plain: The safety exit is about a third of a normal hourly swing, so it gets hit by wiggles.
In 10,000 replays the exit was hit first about 7 times out of 10; the first goal only about 2 times out of 10.
The buy price is below the market, so it may only fill if the stock keeps sliding.
The goals sit under lines where sellers have been showing up all day.
Some of Bull's chart numbers are out of date.
conditions_to_reconsider: A plan with a stop at least about 1x the hourly swing (about $3.85 away) that still pays 1.5x or more, and desk replays moving toward the target. Or price holding above the session VWAP (about $171.75) for an hour on rising volume, or the board giving a clear result. Safest: wait until after the Nov 17 earnings.
